findings.problem: Same regression as the 'No recent activity' filter, one step downstream. Before the remediation a deal inactive for 30 days or more published 'Stalled 45 days', which matched. It now publishes 'No recorded activity for 45 days', which matches nothing in the pattern ('no activity' needs the two words together). The longest-inactive deals therefore drop out of the group, while deals at 7 to 29 days ('14 days since last recorded activity') stay in. The test fixture still uses 'Stalled 42 days' (src/dashboard/today/lib/adapters.test.ts:91), so the test passes.

Verbatim Batch 03 replacement for "Pre-mortem" (B3-X-066); says what the linked area does.
Verbatim Batch 03 replacement for "Pre-mortem a deal" (B3-X-069).

Stage name in the Stage menu. 'PoC' is the ordinary sales abbreviation for proof of concept and is paired with the plain word Pilot; AUDIT_BRIEF §3 disputed terms (proof): ordinary 'proof of concept' is not the retired product noun.
Loss-reason option the seller picks. Ordinary business idiom for a cancelled budget; it is not a state the product assigns and not Antaeus vocabulary. A newcomer understands it.
Section heading over Use case, Pain, Competition, Decision process, Notes. Common informal sales English for information about the deal; no Antaeus-specific meaning.

Empty state. 'yet' marks that the list can be filled, in the same way as the approved Batch 03 replacements 'Not confirmed yet.' and 'No event search has been run yet.'; it is not a judgment about the reader. 'Mapped' is the ordinary sales term (stakeholder mapping).

Matches the approved Batch 03 wording ('21 days since last recorded activity'). The number is days since the deal record was last updated (deal.updated_at); 'recorded' keeps the claim to what the product knows and does not say the buyer went silent.

retained.why: Verbatim Batch 03 / interaction-patch replacement (B3-X-065, first sentence of HS-040). Names the action; 'next step' is standard sales language.

Caption under the dollar total of open deals outside the lower-risk band. Number plus unit plus state; the headline beside it says what the risk is based on.
